findings: The implementation row order remains row0=A-only/old, row1=B-only/tail, row2=both, whereas the source table displays B-only first. The zero/one product theorems apply their corresponding actual interior equivalences, with no row swap. Their arbitrary D0,H0,tD,tH scope is valid because a section-image triple never contains both occurrences.

tripleLift has two distinct exceptional cases: middle=A and upper=B reads the collapsed lower entry; lower=A and middle=B reads the collapsed upper entry. All other triples use the actual collapsed core triple. The reviewed code uses tripleLift_upper only for the A gate and tripleLift_lower only for the B gate, matching the source near-data prescription.

spanning_zero_gate_values evaluates the actual old-image near and far triples at every core interior cut, and spanning_one_gate_values evaluates the actual tail images. The section lemmas prove absence of both occurrences and exact recovery of all three collapsed entries. These are pointwise identities for the actual cut-set gate functions, not assumed weight correspondences.

For an inherited both-row cut with x.val=s, Subtype.ext identifies x with the actual spanningCoreCut. The actual A near triple is (old(L),A,B). The upper exceptional lift gives t(collapse(old(L)))=t(L), and spanning_coreNear_value identifies the actual core near gate at s with precisely t(L). The result needs the source auxiliary coreNear specialization, which is explicit in the inherited both-row theorem; it is not incorrectly generalized to arbitrary D0.

For inherited cuts off s, the proof splits x<s and s<x. It uses the previously proved old near triple on the left and tail near triple on the right, followed by the corresponding section-value theorem. This retains the physically different adjacent occurrence at the right neighbor while giving the same core near value. The far value uses the old section image for every inherited cut, including A.

The additional B near triple is exactly (A,B,tail(R)); the lower exceptional lift reads t(collapse(tail(R)))=t(R). Its actual far triple is the tail image of C.farAtCut at the distinguished core cut s, so its far value is H0(X,s,Y). The generic far exceptional data u does not enter this value because this far triple is a section image, containing only B among the duplicate occurrences.

Each one-cut product is reindexed through the complete actual interior-cut Equiv, and pointwise near/far equalities replace every factor. Fintype.prod_sum_type and the unique Unit product yield (t(R)-H0(coreFar(s)))/2 times the complete core gate product.
